newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil off with futures in dull market.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil off with futures in dull market.

text.p: NWE gas oil edged lower on Thursday in line with hefty benchmark gas oil future losses, traders said.
June IPE settled $3.0 lower at $165.70 a tonne, while the July contract settled at $2.75 off at $167.75 a tonne.

The barge market was described as "dismal" with buyers and sellers wide apart. Heating oil barge premiums were quoted at June IPE +25 cents/+$1.25 fob ARA. There was talk that some deals had been done at June IPE +75 cents and +$1.0, although this was not confimed.
The cargo market was also fairly quiet.
A cargo of German DIN was reported to have traded at July IPE +25 cents cif NWE for June 20-30 delivery.
Russian material, meanwhile, was quoted at June IPE +50 cents/$1.50 a tonne.
Low sulphur was steady although no demand was heard and Med cargoes continued to weigh on the NWE market.

"The spread's still wide enough to make it worth while to bring Med material this way but there's not that much low sulphur available now until the end of June," said one trader. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
